The session itself is a repair. Midday marked 63,273.4 with the three-day range floor at 63,309.4 freshly broken on a settled 1H close and price retesting it from underneath. Since then price fell once more to 63,115.0 on the 18:30Z 15m bar - 268.3 points beneath the broken floor and the lowest print since the flush - and then rallied 530.4 points to a 63,645.4 high on the 22:15Z bar before settling back to 63,519.1. Six consecutive settled 1H closes now sit ABOVE the 63,309.4 floor: 63,311.6, 63,412.9, 63,417.7, 63,478.9, 63,531.6, 63,478.9. The breakdown has been reclaimed on the tape. What it has not done is get through anything: spot at 63,519.1 sits 1.4 points under the 1H EMA20 at 63,520.47, which is the single tightest standoff on the board.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H close back below $63,309.4 - the three-day range floor that broke on the 16:00Z bar and has since been reclaimed by six consecutive settled closes. The level has changed roles twice in nine hours and that is precisely why it is the trigger: it was support through 11-13 August, it became resistance when the 16:00Z bar settled 63,165.1 beneath it, and it is support again now. A third role change - a settled close back underneath - would say the reclaim was a dead-cat bounce inside a broken structure rather than a repair, and it would do so with the 63,115.0 session low only 194.4 points further down and the 62,846.3 flush low 463.1 below that. Note this is a genuine settle condition, not a wick: the 18:30Z 15m bar traded 63,115.0 and the 1H bar containing it still settled 63,311.6, above the line, which is the whole reason the floor counts as reclaimed.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H close above $63,672.0 - the 1H EMA50 at 63,671.95 - with aggregate BTC open interest NOT rising across the same bar. The open-interest condition is carried forward for the sixth consecutive session because it keeps separating a move that is being bought from one that is being covered, and this session is the clearest illustration yet of why that matters: the entire 530-point rally off 63,115.0 was accompanied by open interest FALLING 0.58% and by $591,179 of short liquidations, which is covering, not accumulation. The price gate has moved DOWN from midday's 63,625.2 for a mechanical reason, not a loosening of standards: the 1H EMA20 that midday used as the gate has fallen from 63,625.17 to 63,520.47 and spot is now sitting on it, so it no longer discriminates anything. The next average that does is the EMA50 at 63,671.95, 152.9 points overhead, and behind it the 4H EMA200 at 63,717.49. A settled close above the EMA50 without an open-interest build would be the first evidence since 11 August that someone is actually buying this.

decisionBox.changed: Position moves from midday's HOLD to REDUCE, and the futures book is flat because midday's short was stopped out. Both changes need explaining honestly because one of them is a loss. FIRST, the stop. Midday opened a 60 USDT 2x short at 63,273.4 with the stop at 63,580, chosen to sit above the 16:00Z bar high of 63,571.4 and just under the then-1H EMA20. The 22:15Z 15m bar printed 63,645.4, 65.4 points through it, and the trade was stopped for roughly -29 cents. The level was not badly chosen - it was 1.06 hourly ATRs away and it was above the structure it needed to be above - it was simply the wrong direction, and the report should say so plainly rather than dress it up. SECOND, the REDUCE. This is NOT a repeat of morning's mistake of selling into weakness; it is the opposite trade and it is deliberate. Morning trimmed 17% at 63,476.3 into a falling tape. Midday explicitly refused to sell the low of a completed flush at 63,273.4, and that refusal was correct - price is 245.7 points higher. This session sells a small slice into STRENGTH, at 63,519.1, into the underside of the 1H EMA20, after a 530-point bounce, with an overnight gap ahead and no report until roughly 02:00. The evidence for taking something off here rather than adding: every 1H exponential average is still overhead - EMA20 63,520.47 by 1.4 points, EMA50 63,671.95, EMA100 63,909.34, EMA200 63,991.41 - and every 4H average too, with the 4H EMA200 at 63,717.49 that midday watched fail still 198.4 points above. The daily is unchanged and unrepaired: no new settled daily bar has printed since midday, so all four daily averages remain overhead with the EMA200 at 72,450.33, 14.1% above spot, and the daily MACD line still beneath zero at -45.15. Positioning is the sharpest argument: the OKX long/short account ratio has sat at 1.87-1.88 through the entire bounce and printed 1.88 on the 00:00Z read, the highest of the day. A 530-point rally that does not reduce retail long crowding is a rally that has flushed nobody, and the fuel that produced the 16:00Z break is all still there. Set against that, the constructive case is real and is why the trim is SMALL rather than a full exit: the 1H MACD histogram has crossed positive at +0.37 for the first time since the breakdown, the 4H 16:00Z bar settled 63,412.9 as a long-legged hammer with a 566.6-point lower wick, and the 20:00Z bar settled higher again at 63,478.9. The book is being reduced, not reversed.

overnightRisk: The gap between this report and the next is roughly six hours of thin book, and the specific shape of the risk is unusually legible tonight. FIRST and most concrete: the liquidation map is lopsided in a way that matters. Measured over the 16:40Z-00:02Z window, $1,446,868 of realized liquidation mass sits BELOW spot against $98,319 above, a 14.7-to-1 imbalance, with the two heaviest shelves at 62,800 ($478,333) and 62,900 ($473,886). That mass is consumed liquidity, not resting orders, so it does not pull price by itself - but it marks the corridor the 16:00Z flush already carved out, and a move that re-enters it has a proven path down to 62,846.3 with nothing measured in the way between 63,100 and 62,900 except $5,016 and $4,774 in the 63,100 and 63,200 buckets. That is a thin shelf directly beneath the reduce line, and it is why the resting stop at 63,290 is recommended rather than optional. SECOND: retail positioning is the loaded spring. The long/short account ratio closed the day at 1.88, its high, after sitting 1.87-1.88 through a 530-point rally. Longs added into the flush this afternoon and did not take profit into the bounce this evening. If the 63,309.4 reclaim fails while the book is that crowded, the same mechanism that produced a 1,153-point round trip today is available again, and overnight liquidity is a fraction of the US-session liquidity that absorbed it. THIRD: the calendar. No US ETF flow figure has posted for 13 August - the Farside table still ends at 12 August with -$61.1m - so that number lands during or just before the next session and is a live unknown rather than a settled fact. Funding settles again at 08:00Z. FOURTH: the cross-asset setup is the most uncomfortable it has been all week. QQQ closed +1.16% at 732.07 and VOO closed +0.67% at 714.95 with an intraday high of 716.39 that IS its 52-week high, so the US market went out at a record on a soft PPI print while Bitcoin spent the day repairing a broken range floor. If that risk-on bid persists overnight in Asia - JP225 is already +1.55% - Bitcoin's failure to participate becomes a relative-strength indictment rather than a coincidence. FIFTH, the smaller tail: Brent fell 2.12% to 87.09 with the Strait of Hormuz impasse unresolved and the IEA cutting demand forecasts; an energy headline in either direction moves the dollar and the whole risk complex, and DXY at 99.918 is close enough to 100 that a break through it would be read as a regime signal. The single line to watch is 63,309.4 on a settled 1H close. Above it the repair stands and the overnight is likely chop between there and 63,672. Below it the map beneath is thin until 62,900.

liquidation.note: $478,333 and the heaviest bucket on this window's map. It is built entirely from the 16:5xZ flush - long positions force-sold between 62,821.8 and 62,878.1 - and it sits 719.1 points below spot. Read it correctly: this is REALIZED mass, liquidity that has already been consumed, not resting orders waiting below. Its value is as a marker of the corridor the flush carved and as the floor of the region a failed reclaim would revisit. It is flagged as the magnet because it is the single largest cluster and because it sits directly beneath the thin 63,100-63,200 shelf, which is where a break would accelerate.

$473,886, effectively a twin of the 62,800 bucket and contiguous with it. Together the 62,800-62,900 band carries $952,219, which is 61.6% of all liquidation mass measured this window. Both were created inside the same four-minute cascade between 16:54Z and 16:56Z. The largest single fill in the band is 164.69 contracts at 62,930.7.

$303,573 and the informative bucket on this map, because unlike the two beneath it this one is SHORT liquidations, not long. It is dominated by a single 382.33-contract fill at 63,476.3 worth $242,689 that printed at 19:08:28Z, as price was climbing back through the broken floor. Shorts that positioned for continuation after the 16:00Z settle were force-covered 128 points later. It sits 119.1 points below spot and marks where the bounce got its fuel.

$119,937, again short liquidations, clustered at 63,310.5 and 63,328.8 with fills timestamped 19:0xZ. That is the reclaim of the 63,309.4 floor being fought and won, priced. It sits 219.1 points below spot and directly on the reduce trigger.

$61,349, straddling spot at 63,519.1 - fills range from 63,514.1 up to 63,579.9, all short liquidations from the 22:1xZ push. Classified below because the bucket floor sits under spot. $5,016. This is the thin shelf and it is the most operationally important small number on the page. Between the 63,300 bucket and the 62,900 bucket there is almost nothing measured: $4,774 at 63,200 and $5,016 at 63,100, together under $10,000 against $952,219 sitting below at 62,800-62,900. Midday reported this band as heavily filled on its 24-hour window; on this evening's shorter window that older mass has rolled out and what remains is a near-vacuum. A settled break of 63,309.4 walks into it.

$4,774, the other half of the thin shelf. Short liquidations at 63,206.4, 63,216.3 and 63,220.5 from the 17:50Z recovery, nothing else. Same caveat as 63,100: this reads thin partly because the window is shorter than midday's, not because the older mass was erased from the tape.

liquidityMagnet.note: IMPORTANT WINDOW CAVEAT, stated up front so the numbers are not misread against midday's. The larger limit values on this endpoint exceeded the tool's response ceiling and had to be dropped to limit=11, so this map covers 2026-08-13T16:40:56Z to 2026-08-14T00:02:55Z - seven hours and twenty-two minutes - against midday's full 24-hour, 799-fill window. Totals are therefore NOT comparable to midday's and no attempt is made to compare them. Within this window: 175 fills, $954,008 of long liquidations against $591,179 of shorts, ratio 1.61. Freshness is not in doubt - the newest fill printed at 63,442.1 at 00:02:55Z, 77 points from spot and 42 minutes before the read. The shape is the story and it is genuinely two-sided, which is unusual for this desk to be able to say. The first third of the window is one direction: longs liquidated between 62,821.8 and 62,979.2 in a four-minute cascade at 16:5xZ, $952,219 of it in the 62,800-62,900 band. The last two thirds are the other direction: shorts liquidated continuously from 63,155.9 at 17:49Z all the way up to 63,614.4 at 22:16Z, including a single 382.33-contract fill at 63,476.3 worth $242,689. The flush and the squeeze both happened, in that order, inside one evening. Pull is marked DOWN on the raw arithmetic - $1,446,868 below spot against $98,319 above, 14.7-to-1 - but that ratio overstates the case and should be read with the standing caveat that this is consumed liquidity by construction: mass accumulates below precisely BECAUSE price fell through it. The honest operational reading is narrower: there is a measured near-vacuum between 63,100 and 63,200 totalling under $10,000, and a wall of consumed supply at 62,800-62,900. A settled loss of 63,309.4 has thin air for roughly two hundred points and then a shelf.

timeframes.structure: The decisive timeframe, and it has produced the session's one genuinely constructive signal alongside the session's tightest standoff. The signal: the MACD histogram has crossed POSITIVE at +0.37, line -68.93 against signal -69.30 - the first bullish cross on this timeframe since the breakdown, and the exact mirror of the bearish cross midday recorded at -33.59. The standoff: spot at 63,519.1 sits 1.4 points beneath the EMA20 at 63,520.47. Not above, not meaningfully below - on it. RSI has recovered from 36.81 to 47.39, a 10.6-point repair that unwinds the oversold condition without reaching anything that could be called strength. The settled close sequence since midday is the cleanest evidence the reclaim is real: 63,146.4, 63,311.6, 63,412.9, 63,417.7, 63,478.9, 63,531.6, 63,478.9 - one lower close, then six consecutive settles above the 63,309.4 floor, five of them above the 63,412.9 level too. Against that, the structure overhead is untouched: EMA50 63,671.95 is 152.9 points up, EMA100 63,909.34 is 390.2 up, EMA200 63,991.41 is 472.3 up, and all four remain stacked in bearish order. A timeframe that has repaired its momentum but reclaimed none of its averages is a timeframe in the middle of a range, which is what the overall bias says.

timeframes.structure: Midday left one explicit open question on this timeframe and it has been answered constructively. The forming 16:00Z bar was described as a long-legged hammer with a 427.1-point lower wick that would be the first constructive candle in three days IF it settled near where it was trading. It settled 63,412.9 - above its 63,416.7 open by a whisker under, but 566.6 points above its 62,846.3 low and only 158.5 below its high, which is a textbook hammer close in the upper third of the range. The 20:00Z bar that followed settled higher again at 63,478.9. Two consecutive constructive 4H settles, the first such pair since 11 August. The oscillators confirm the improvement without overstating it: RSI up from 39.89 to 41.33, MACD histogram narrowing from -23.82 to -12.77 with the line ticking up from -272.87 to -269.40. But the repair is entirely internal to the candles, not to the structure: the EMA200 at 63,717.49 - the line whose loss on two consecutive settles killed midnight's reclaim thesis - is still 198.4 points overhead and has not been challenged, the session high of 63,645.4 stopped 72.1 points short of it, and the EMA20/50/100 remain stacked above at 63,803.08, 64,084.69 and 64,131.15. The forming 00:00Z bar opened 63,479.0 and trades 63,519.1.

The skew field carries the OKX long/short ACCOUNT ratio at 1.88 (00:00Z read) per the field's definition, and it is the most bearish number in this report. The evening's hourly series reads 1.79, 1.80, 1.84, 1.87, 1.88, 1.87, 1.87, 1.87, 1.88, 1.87, 1.88 - it rose into the flush, and then it did NOT fall during a 530-point rally. Supporting the same read from the other side, the book keeps shrinking rather than levering up: BTC-USDT-SWAP open interest is $2,043,838,880 at the 00:39:14Z read against midday's $2,055,737,216, -0.58%, and the entire bounce off 63,115.0 was accompanied by falling open interest, which makes it short-covering rather than accumulation. calibration.rollingRecord: 2 of the last 10 rated sessions helped. The two yes marks remain 12 August midnight and 13 August morning; 11 August morning/midday/endday, 12 August morning/midday/endday, 13 August midnight and now 13 August midday are all no. The pattern across ten sessions is consistent enough to be worth naming: the published LEVELS have been good and the TRADES taken at the mark have been poor. This session repeats it exactly - both midday levels held their definitions and neither fired, while the trade placed between them lost.
calibration.note: Neither of midday's published levels fired, and the trade taken between them was stopped out. Taking them in order. The REDUCE line at 62,846.3 required a settled 1H close below the flush low; the lowest print since was 63,115.0 on the 18:30Z 15m bar and the lowest settled 1H close was 63,146.4, so the line was missed by 268.7 points on prints and 300.1 on settles. It was never close. The ADD line at 63,625.2 - the 1H EMA20 - required a settled 1H close above with open interest not rising. Price reached 63,645.4 on the 22:15Z 15m bar, 20.2 points through the level, but the 1H bar containing it settled 63,531.6, so the settle condition correctly withheld the signal. Both lines therefore did their jobs by declining to fire, and the composite trigger's settle requirement spared a bad long exactly as it was designed to. The TRADE is the negative and it is unambiguous. Midday opened a 60 USDT 2x futures short at 63,273.4 with the stop at 63,580, sized at 1.06 hourly ATRs and placed above the 16:00Z bar high of 63,571.4. The 22:15Z bar traded 63,645.4 and the stop filled for roughly -$0.29 on the wallet, about -0.15% of net worth. The reasoning behind the short was internally sound - the range floor had genuinely broken on a settle, every 1H average was overhead, the 1H MACD had crossed negative, the daily MACD had gone sub-zero, and realized long liquidations were running at nearly 3x shorts - but it was a continuation bet placed at the retest of a level that then held, in a range that had already produced a 1,153-point round trip that same afternoon. The transferable lesson is narrower than 'do not short': after a completed liquidation cascade, the retest of the broken level is the WORST location for a continuation entry, because that is precisely where the shorts who are about to be squeezed are positioned. The tape proved it - $591,179 of short liquidations printed between 17:49Z and 22:16Z, and the single largest at 63,476.3 was 203 points above midday's entry. The desk's own short was on the same side as the crowd that got run over. Set against the loss, one thing was right and is worth banking: midday refused to sell the spot core into the low of the flush at 63,273.4, and spot is 245.7 points higher. Holding the core was the correct half of a two-part decision whose other half lost.

sources.title: DATA-ACCESS NOTE for the next run — three findings. (1) /market/ticker is still serving the SAME pinned body midday rejected (ts 2026-08-13T11:21:41Z, last 63,607.8), now 13.5 hours stale, and it survives cache-busting query params because the proxy strips them from that path. Treat the ticker endpoint as dead. (2) The proxy caches per-URL, so /market/candles with a limit value no prior run has used returns LIVE data — limit=300 came back stale (newest bar 07:00Z) while limit=287, 93, 89, 31 and 11 were all live. Always vary the limit and always difference the newest bar ts against wall clock. (3) The Claude-in-Chrome browser fallback midday recommended was NOT available this run (extension not connected), and the sandbox shell has no network at all (proxy returns 403 for okx.com, api.kraken.com, stockanalysis.com and everything else tested), so web_fetch is the only path. Kraken /0/public/Ticker and Coinbase /v2/prices are both reachable via web_fetch and make good independent spot cross-checks.
